evidence.description: Public initializer in a class with a shared instance.

candidates.explanation: The class uses a singleton pattern but includes a public initializer, which allows for the creation of multiple instances of a class intended to be a singleton.
candidates.title: Public Initializer in Singleton

evidence.description: Instantiation of ISO8601DateFormatter inside a method.

candidates.explanation: The `lastUpdatedDate` method creates a new instance of `ISO8601DateFormatter` every time it is called. Date formatters are expensive to initialize and should be reused.
candidates.title: Expensive DateFormatter Instantiation

evidence.description: Separate properties for value and date for treesPlanted and totalInvestments.

candidates.explanation: The class uses multiple properties to store related data (e.g., a value and its last updated date) instead of grouping them into a single structure, which can lead to state inconsistency.
candidates.title: Data Grouping Smells

evidence.description: Manual mapping of results to class properties via switch statement.

candidates.explanation: The `fetchAndUpdate` method performs a large switch statement to manually map array elements to specific properties. This logic is tightly coupled to the structure of the JSON response.
candidates.title: Tight Coupling in Data Mapping
